en: In the work *Saṅgītamālikā* composed by Dr. Śrīyut Indravimala Caturdhurīṇa concerning Yaśodharā, the first song is the "Hymn to the Illustrious Yaśodharā": 1. O Mother, support of the world, who gladdens the hearts of devotees, who removes the veil [of worldly illusion], and who caused your son to renounce the world—to you, salutations! (1.116)
O Mother Yaśodharā, of vast renown, who removes the torment of sin, resplendent like gold, enchanting to the Sugata, as delicate as a flower—grant me your foot upon the forehead of the Lord of Sages.

O Mother Bimbisundarī, O Gopī Amba Bhaddakacce, O Subhaddakā! When the fruit of sacred learning has become fruitless on this earth, [only] you—who move upon the path of love, who are stainless through merit, sweet with poetry, and radiant with the scriptures—Yati worships once again at your lotus feet. 3.3 Bimbisundarī, Gopī, Mother, Bhaddakacce, Subhaddakā!
Homage to you, O essence of compassion,
the mother of Rāhula!
Homage to you. 4.119.

The Second Council: The Birth of Yaśodharā. "Homage to the Blessed One, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One. When the Tathāgata arrived in the city of Kapilavastu with a shower of moonbeam-like rays, on the full-moon day of Vaiśākha, the heat of sin was long since washed away, and the divine song arose: "He who has abandoned all strife is born!"

Then you too, O Mother, who wards off the suffering of worldly existence, became the charming daughter Yaśodharā— possessor of fame, the delight of the minds of all people, and the protector of cowherds from the fear of painful separation.

In the descent as Rāma, you were Sītā, the Mother of the World and daughter of the Earth; now you have come again in age after age as a cowherd girl, a Mother whose mind is intent on removing the sins of the world. Chandaka has been born as your long-time charioteer, Kaṇṭhaka as your horse who moves with the speed of thought, and others as your playful companions—oh, how they purify the earth!
The great joy that brings long-lasting auspiciousness.
All those dear attendants arrived at the very same time.
O Mother, grant us your blessings as you recount your divine play;
the ascetic leads the Tathāgata along with you again and again.
Third Song: On the day of the wedding, O Mother Yaśodharā, whose sole life is the Blessed Buddha—homage be to you!
O you who were beautifully smiling and prepared for the wedding day—homage be to you! (1) 124.
The supreme creation of the Creator, the ultimate refuge of the Buddha alone, she was intent on saying: "I shall adorn Māra, but not you. (2.125)

The celestial chariots of Hatāśa, Sundarānanda, and Devadatta were destroyed; meanwhile, the great glory of the bamboo-pipe was bound [in place], signaling the approaching arrival of Maitreya. || 3 || 126 ||
O you who bring about the great awakening of the great power of the Dharma and the Saṅgha;
O Daṇḍapāṇi-Mahāmāyā, bestower of supreme bliss! (4) 127.
O Mother Gopī, who dwells upon the earth, grant virtuous intellect to your sons, for mortals are crushed by machines and filled with fear of violence and other evils. (5) 128.
O purifier of the Kali age, O Great Mother, salutations to you;
let there be salutations to you, the excellent protector of this lowest of sons, the Lord of Ascetics. 6 || 129 ||
The fourth council was a source of happiness, bringing certain blossoming to its mother;
it was the illumination of truth in a world afflicted by defilements. || 1 || 130 ||
Oh, how great is the earth’s terror! || 2 || 232 ||
The laughter that pulverizes the Āṇava-knot, the exultation that destroys the Dānavas, the bursting asunder of Rudra, and the sport of Antaka. || 3 || 132 ||
May there be supreme joy for my mother;
may he be the light of welfare in this world of afflictions. || 4 || 133 ||
May excellent brotherly affection flourish in every direction, increasing the root of merit for the people of the world through the five precepts fully elaborated;
may it establish the universe as eternally pure through the four noble truths and so forth, which ward off the five aggregates. (5) 134.

May the land of Bhārata, which has conquered through truth and dharma the masses of lands such as Siṃhala, Brahmaśyāma, Cīna, Kamboja, and Nīpa, flourish with the songs of mothers and the melodies of the vigil for their sons; may it be blessed with joy from its daughters. 6) 135)
May merit, augmented by meditation, spread forth;
may merit shine incessantly upon the field of action. 136.
O Giver of Boons, O Jewel among Mothers, in this land which is my merit-wealth, may the destruction of fratricidal treachery take place;
O Mother, you are the supreme consolation of the universe. (8) 137.
